newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher on commercial buying.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher on commercial buying.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled higher amid commercial buying, although July was dented at the close as a key buyer turned seller.

Traders said commodity brokerage E.D.& F. Man International, which bought at least two million July bushels and bear-spread one million July/May at 25 cents early in the session, turned seller of 2.6 million July toward the close.
That had the effect of widening the May/July spread, which had fluctuated throughout the session. The spread closed on paper at 27 cents, out from its opening level of 24 cents.

Traders said wheat was generally supported by commercially oriented buying throughout the session. Continental and CIS each purchased around one million July bushels. KCBT wheat also saw spillover strength from commercial buying in Chicago.

"This was the second straight day of commercial buying in Chicago but the first day in Kansas City," a KCBT trader said. "Continued fears surrounding dryness in the hard red winter wheat belt...(also) kept KC firm."

KCBT wheat settled 3-1/4 to 5-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with May up 5-1/4 cents at $4.21-1/2. July, which had been as much as 5-3/4 cents higher earlier in the session, settled up 3-1/4 cents at $3.94-1/2.
